evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: Broken Hill was an electoral district of the Legislative Assembly in the Australian state of New South Wales.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: From 1894 to 1913, the Broken Hill district was covered by the electoral districts of "Broken Hill", Willyama and Sturt.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In the 1912 redistribution, the electoral district of "Broken Hill" was abolished and absorbed into "Willyama" and "Sturt".

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1920, "Willyama", "Sturt" and the electoral district of Cobar were combined to create a three-member "Sturt".

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1927, single-member electorates were recreated and the city of Broken Hill was split between "Sturt" and Murray.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: From 1932, the city of Broken Hill was split between "Sturt" and Cobar.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1968 "Sturt" was renamed Broken Hill and included all of the city of Broken Hill.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Broken Hill
evidence.text: In 1999, it was merged with part of "Murray" and renamed the electoral district of Murray-Darling.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Southern Boroughs
evidence.text: Southern Boroughs was a former electoral district for the Legislative Assembly in the Australian state of New South Wales created in 1856.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Southern Boroughs
evidence.text: It included the towns of Goulburn, Braidwood, Yass and Queanbeyan, while the surrounding rural area were in the electoral districts of Argyle, United Counties of Murray and St Vincent and King and Georgiana.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Southern Boroughs
evidence.text: It was replaced by Goulburn, Braidwood, Queanbeyan and Yass in 1859.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Argyle
evidence.text: Argyle was an electoral district for the Legislative Assembly in the Australian State of New South Wales from 1856 to 1904, including Argyle County surrounding Goulburn.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Argyle
evidence.text: The town of Goulburn was in Southern Boroughs from 1856 to 1859 and then Goulburn.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Goulburn (Victoria)
evidence.text: Electoral district of Goulburn was an electoral district of the Legislative Assembly in the Australian state of Victoria.

evidence.title: Electoral district of Goulburn (Victoria)
evidence.text: It was preceded by the Electoral district of Goulburn Valley, which was abolished in 1945.
